subject: RiskProof — follow-up: non-prod data flow, SIG mapping & evidence schedule
messages:
From: Elena Moss <elena@riskproof.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: RiskProof Security Team <security@riskproof.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RiskProof — evidence & clarifications for SIG questionnaire (non-prod/dataflow)

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks again for taking the time on Friday. As we discussed, our procurement team is trying to close the SIG + ISO/SOC2 assurance tranche ahead of contract signature. We have a few outstanding clarifications and evidence asks focused on non-production environments and how transient customer data is handled during testing and internal validation. At a high level: 

- Can you confirm whether non-prod environments may contain masked copies of customer PII? If yes, what masking process and verification controls exist?
- Please provide a network/data flow diagram that shows: ephemeral storage, backup retention, and any cross-region replication for staging/dev clusters.
- We need the SIG control mapping for the following control families: Encryption, Access Control (IA/Privileged), Logging & Monitoring, Change Management, and Data Retention. A mapping to SOC 2 CC5.x (and ISO 27001 Annex A controls where applicable) would be ideal.
- For evidence, our auditors will accept: redacted SOC 2 report (if available), screenshots of KMS policies/roles, one example of a rotation log for a service key, and a short video walkthrough (screen capture) of the dev cluster provisioning process.

Proposed timeline: we need the control mapping + architecture diagram by EOD Wednesday (7/13) to keep our vendor review on track. Can you confirm ownership and delivery?

Thanks,
Elena Moss
Senior Security Operations Manager
RiskProof
attachments: none (we will upload the SIG questionnaire into your shared folder)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Moss <elena@riskproof.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RiskProof — evidence & clarifications for SIG questionnaire (non-prod/dataflow)

Elena — thanks for the note and the timeline. We can meet the Wednesday EOD ask with a prioritized packet. Quick answers up front:

- Non-prod: we do not keep unmasked customer PII in any non-production environment. Occasionally customers opt-in to a redacted dataset for troubleshooting; in those cases we apply deterministic masking and store artifacts in encrypted buckets with 30-day retention unless a longer window is required for a specific support case.
- Ownership: Marissa (Security & Compliance) will own the SIG/SOC2 mapping and evidence collection. Neha (Assurance Intake) will coordinate artifacts and the shared Drive.

I'm attaching a short checklist and an initial mapping template (SIG->SOC2->ISO) that should speed handoffs. We'll push the architecture diagram and a signed redacted SOC2 by tomorrow EOD. If RiskProof needs a live walkthrough, Marissa can host a 30-minute session Thursday morning.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Customer Security
Redwood Inference
attachments: karthik/initial-sig-checklist.xlsx

Karthik — that works. Two follow-ups from our side: 

1) For rotation logs — do you have an exported CSV or a timestamped audit trail we can ingest? Our auditors prefer an exportable artifact (CSV/JSON) over screenshots.
2) For the network/dataflow diagram, could you explicitly note ephemeral storage boundaries (e.g., /tmp, ephemeral pod volumes) and confirm whether ephemeral logs are retained beyond 24 hours without explicit ingestion to centralized logging?

If you can add both items to the packet tomorrow, we should be able to move to a short intake call on Thursday.

— RiskProof Security
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Moss <elena@riskproof.com>, security@riskproof.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 12 Jul 2028 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RiskProof — evidence & clarifications for SIG questionnaire (non-prod/dataflow)

Elena / RiskProof team — attaching the requested artifacts per Karthik's checklist. Highlights and clarifications below. Attachments: nonprod-arch-v1.png (diagram), soc2-rep-redacted.pdf (redacted attestation), rotation-export-20280711.csv (KMS/service key rotation export). We also included a short readme with evidence provenance.

Key clarifications:
- Masking: non-prod datasets that are used for debugging are generated from production extracts via a deterministic masking library we maintain internally. The masking run has a generated checksum and is logged; the checksum is included in the evidence readme.
- Ephemeral storage: ephemeral pod volumes are ephemeral and not backed up. Logs are shipped to our centralized logging (ELK) by a sidecar; ephemeral logs that are not ingested are auto-deleted within 24 hours. The architecture diagram annotates the sidecar and log retention policy.
- Rotation export: the CSV contains timestamp, key-id, rotated-by (service account), and rotation-type. We redacted the column with full key material.

We have also recorded a 6-minute video walkthrough of the dev cluster provisioning process — link in the Drive folder. If RiskProof prefers, we can provide an ingestion-friendly CSV for the rotation logs (instead of the attached export).

Proposed next step: can we schedule a 30-minute call Thursday 9:00–9:30 PT for a quick intake review? Any other artifacts we should include in the packet?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Security Programs Manager
Redwood Inference

Marissa / Karthik — thanks for the thorough packet and the quick turnaround. The diagram and the rotation export look good. A couple of final items from our auditor:

- Please add a short MD file that documents the masking algorithm (high-level pseudocode) and points to the checksum you mentioned — they want to tie the masking assertion to a reproducible recipe. No need to include code, just the algorithm name and parameters used for de-identification.
- For the rotation CSV: yes, an ingestion-friendly CSV (without redacted headers) would be ideal. Could you deliver that by Monday EOD?

If you can provide those two small items, we should be able to move to the next stage and schedule the intake call for Thursday as proposed. Appreciate the responsiveness.

Best,
Elena Moss
Senior Security Operations Manager
